chunks: And from him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Samaan, who said:

I asked him about the day in which one is uncertain whether it is from the month of Ramadan or not, and he does not know if it is from Sha'ban or from the month of Ramadan, so he fasted it as from Ramadan. He said: 'It is a day for which he was granted success, and there is no make-up (qada) required for him.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on fasting on the day of doubt at the end of Sha'ban?
ai.summary: This hadith from Sahih al-Tusi establishes the principle of 'Ihtiyat' (precaution) in the entry of Ramadan, where fasting on the day of doubt is accepted as valid Ramadan fasting if the intention is made for Ramadan, thereby exempting the believer from make-up (Qada). It reflects the Shia juristic preference for treating the day as Ramadan to ensure the completeness of the month's worship, avoiding the need for double fasting or uncertainty. This ruling underscores the flexibility in Islamic jurisprudence regarding lunar sighting ambiguities, prioritizing the spiritual benefit of the fast over strict chronological certainty.
